name: Cross-sectional laggard reversion — buy the worst-ranked oversold name (long spot)
rationale: STATISTICAL-ARB / CROSS-SECTIONAL, the REVERSION mirror of every existing xsec-momentum LEADER spec. xsec_momentum_rank is the percentile rank of N-day return across the universe (1 = leader, 0 = laggard). All existing cross-sectional specs go LONG the LEADERS (top rank). This spec exploits the opposite, well-documented short-horizon effect: the EXTREME LAGGARD (bottom-rank) that has also become statistically oversold tends to mean-revert UP relative to the pack as the over-selling exhausts — a single-instrument approximation of a cross-sectional reversal / dispersion-compression trade (no pairs engine needed; the rank IS the relative-value coordinate). Mechanism before data: long spot when xsec_momentum_rank is below a fitted laggard floor (worst relative performers) AND RSI is oversold (the over-selling is mechanical, ripe to snap) AND realized vol is contained (an orderly laggard, not a name in terminal collapse); exit on rank recovery via RSI or barriers. Distinct from cross-asset-social-rotation and xsec-neutral-momentum-long-leg (both buy LEADERS). Disconfirmer 1: drop the rank arm — if a bare oversold RSI dip-buy matches the deflated Sharpe, the cross-sectional laggard coordinate adds nothing. Disconfirmer 2: laggards can be laggards for a reason (terminal decline); if requiring the LOWEST rank makes the edge worse than a mid-rank dip, this is value-trap risk, not reversion. Disconfirmer 3 (PIT/cost): rank is PIT (instruments present at bar close); net of ~20bps the relative bounce must clear. tier0 xsec_momentum_rank + tier0 rsi/vol, computed-at-backtest, unproven combination — low-confidence until OOS.
catalyst: an asset at the BOTTOM of the cross-sectional momentum rank that is also oversold in a contained-vol regime — a laggard reversion, long spot
